title: Chandrayaan-3 in 60 seconds

test.captions: big centre words, a few at a time

segments.say: No country had ever landed this close to the Moon's south pole. Until the twenty-third of August, 2023.
Chandrayaan-3 lifted off from Sriharikota on the fourteenth of July, on an LVM3 rocket.
Forty days later, the Vikram lander touched down.
India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, and the first near its south pole.
Why the south pole? Some craters there never see sunlight. They may hold water ice.
Then the Pragyan rover rolled out. It drove about a hundred metres, and confirmed sulphur in the soil.
Vikram even hopped: it lifted about forty centimetres, and landed again.
The landing spot is called Shiv Shakti point. And the twenty-third of August is now National Space Day.

sources: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 mission page and press releases, Jul–Sep 2023: launch 14 Jul 2023 (LVM3-M4), landing 23 Aug 2023, rover traverse ~100 m, LIBS confirmed sulphur, Vikram hop 3 Sep 2023 (~40 cm)
PIB, 26 Aug 2023: landing site named Shiv Shakti point; 23 August declared National Space Day
